cells.title: Refuse reads and commands that touch another project's tree
cells.action: Keep contract cc1d4957 (docs/history/cross-project-guard/CONTEXT.md D1-D4). Add write_guard/cross_project.rs with a check that, given this project's roots, the hook cwd and a candidate path, returns the other project's root when the path belongs to another project per D1: resolve the path (absolute, cwd-relative, or ~ expanded from HOME); it is this project when it is under the store/main root or under a directory whose .git resolves to the same git common dir (this repo's worktrees); otherwise walk up from the path to the nearest ancestor holding .git or .bee/onboarding.json, never counting HOME or / as a root; a different root means another project; a directory that is in no repo but has a direct child holding .git or .bee/onboarding.json (not this project) also counts. Allowed despite a match (D4): a path under any entry of guards.cross_project_allow in .bee/config.json (absolute or ~ prefixes), under any permissions.additionalDirectories entry of ~/.claude/settings.json, <root>/.claude/settings.json or <root>/.claude/settings.local.json, or a harness-allowlisted target (hook_local.rs harness_allowlisted_target). In main.rs run the check after the hook_enabled switch and before the AskUserQuestion/read/write branches, for every phase: Read uses file_path; Glob and Grep use path, and an absolute Glob pattern prefix; Bash/exec checks the hook cwd and every token from tokenize_deep(fence_heredocs(command)) that starts with / or ~ (strip a leading key= of --flag=value tokens). The first hit denies with exit 2 and a message that starts with 'bee cross-project guard:', names the path and the other project root, says not to read or work it from this session, and gives the remedy: waggledance_ask_state for that project, then waggledance_dispatch with leader: true; if the user asked to research that repo from here, ask the user to add the path to guards.cross_project_allow in .bee/config.json. Make guards.cross_project_allow a governed key: extend config_governed_change_deny so bee config set and an agent Edit/Write that adds or changes it are refused like the other governed keys. Red first in write_guard/tests.rs with test names containing cross_project: Read of a file in a sibling fixture repo is refused with the remedy; Grep path at a folder whose child is a repo is refused; Bash 'cat <sibling>/x' and 'cd <sibling> && ls' are refused; Bash with hook cwd inside the sibling is refused; in-repo Read, /tmp Read, a sibling worktree of this repo, a path under guards.cross_project_allow, and a path under a fixture permissions.additionalDirectories entry are all allowed; the check runs while phase is idle; bee config set guards.cross_project_allow is refused. Watch them fail before the fix. Knowledge delta in the same commit: add a cross-project section to docs/knowledge/areas/hook-runtime/write-guard-request-shapes.md citing docs/history/cross-project-guard/CONTEXT.md D1-D4 (not the raw decision id). No code comments. One commit.

truths: A Read, Glob, Grep or Bash call that touches another repo's tree is refused with exit 2 and the waggledance remedy
In-repo paths, this repo's worktrees, no-repo paths, guards.cross_project_allow entries and Claude additionalDirectories entries stay allowed
The refusal fires in every phase, idle included, for leaders and workers
bee config set cannot add guards.cross_project_allow

artifacts.substantive: the D1 ownership check and the D4 allowances
red-first cross_project tests for every D1-D4 case

key_links: main.rs calls the cross-project check before the read and write branches
prohibitions: Never weaken an existing read, privacy or write check
Never let an environment variable turn the check off
open_choices: Cache the walked roots per hook call

cells.title: Add the other-project-to-its-leader doctrine rule
cells.action: Keep contract cc1d4957 (docs/history/cross-project-guard/CONTEXT.md D5, D3, D4). In packages/bee/LEADER.md, section Work in parallel, coordinate through the store, add a marked rule block <!-- rule: agents-other-project-to-its-leader --> ... <!-- /rule -->: work that belongs to another project goes to that project's leader through waggledance — waggledance_ask_state for that project, then waggledance_dispatch with leader: true (follow_up_of when its leader already runs the same work); the session never reads, searches or explores that project's code, and the write-guard refuses it; a research read of another repo needs the user to add it to guards.cross_project_allow. Regenerate the vendored copy with the repo's regen command (bee dev regen) so .bee/LEADER.md matches. Add the rule to the rule index in the router-triage doc beside agents-feedback-changes-framework, same shape: home, spoken line citing cross-project-guard D5, applied_at. Add guards.cross_project_allow to docs/config-reference.md: list of absolute or ~ path prefixes, governed (user edits only), with Claude permissions.additionalDirectories also allowed. ASD-STE100 style, no bee jargon beyond rule ids. One commit.
cells.verify: .bee/bin/bee knowledge check && cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --bin bee -- doctrine

truths: packages/bee/LEADER.md and .bee/LEADER.md carry rule agents-other-project-to-its-leader
The rule index lists it with home, spoken line and applied_at
docs/config-reference.md documents guards.cross_project_allow as governed
key_links: the rule names the write-guard refusal and the waggledance remedy
prohibitions: No hand edit of .bee/LEADER.md beyond the regen output

cells.title: Check relative .. path tokens in Bash against the cross-project rule
cells.action: Keep contracts 118414b3 and a239cdf4. Today the Bash cross-project scan in main.rs and cross_project.rs checks only tokens starting with / or ~, so 'cat ../../anphabe/a-blog/package.json' run from the beehive worktree exits 0. Extend the scan: a Bash token that is a relative path containing a .. segment (also the value of a --flag=value token) is resolved against the hook cwd and checked by the same rule; walk the command's cd tokens in order so a relative token after a relative cd (cd ../y && cat z) resolves against the cd target; a cd to an absolute target resets the base. Relative tokens without .. stay unchecked, as today. Red first in write_guard/tests.rs, names containing cross_project: 'cat ../../<sibling>/x' refused; 'cd ../<sibling-parent> && cat <sibling>/x' refused; 'cat ../<this-repo-dir>/AGENTS.md' resolving into this repo is allowed; 'cat src/../AGENTS.md' allowed. Watch them fail first. Update the cross-project section of write-guard-request-shapes.md (cite CONTEXT.md D2). No code comments. One commit.

truths: A Bash relative token with .. that resolves into another project is refused with the cross-project message
A relative .. token that resolves inside this repo stays allowed
key_links: main.rs hands .. tokens and the cd chain to the cross-project check
